newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemala to place first international bond issue.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala to place first international bond issue.

text.p: Guatemala plans to place a $150 million bond issue in July, its first on the international market, the central bank said on Monday.

"The issue is appropriate for the size of the economy and taking into account that it is really the first time that Guatemala will issue bonds on the international markets," Willy Zapata, president of the Guatemalan central bank, told Reuters.
Zapata said the plan was to issue medium-term bonds that mature in three to five years. The market would determine the rate of the bonds, he said.
The Finance Ministry would choose before the end of the week an investment bank to handle the placement, Zapata said.
According to Zapata the ministry is considering proposals from five investment banks, Lehman Bros., Bank of Boston, Citibank, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell and BZW.
Once a bank is chosen, Zapata said the bonds would be issued about two months later.

An impending country rating by Moody's Investor Services could affect the bond issue, Zapata said. The bond issue will come some weeks after Moody's releases a rating evaluating investment risk in Guatemala.
Zapata said Moody's analysts were in Guatemala in March and the rating committee would decide on a rating by the third week of May.
According to Zapata, Thomson Bank Watch, an institution that rates investment risk in banks and countries, in January raised its Guatemala rating from C to B-.

"This is consistent with the rise in confidence in international markets and it is directly related to the fact that Guatemala is being seen as a market with development possibilities, especially in the areas of energy and telecommunications," Zapata said.
Government plans to privatize telecommunications and other industries were part of the attraction, he said.
